YOLOv8l is a large variant of the YOLOv8 family and is designed to provide higher 
detection accuracy through deeper feature extraction and stronger learning capability. It 
is widely used in computer vision applications where both speed and precision are 
important. 
In this project, YOLOv8l was trained to detect four important classes: helmet, no-
helmet, rider, and number plate. The model processes images and video frames to 
generate bounding boxes, class labels, and confidence scores. These outputs are further 
used for rider tracking, number plate recognition, and violation monitoring.

4.3.2 Architecture of YOLOv8l 
The architecture of YOLOv8l consists of three major components: Backbone, Neck, and 
Head. These components work together to perform accurate and fast object detection. 
1. Backbone:  
The backbone extracts meaningful visual features from the input image such as 
edges, shapes, textures, and object structures. Since YOLOv8l has a deeper 
backbone, it can capture richer features for improved detection performance.

During training, the model learned to detect four custom classes: helmet, no-helmet, rider, 
and number plate. After successful completion of training, the best -performing weights 
were selected for model evaluation and real-time deployment. 
4.5 MODEL EV ALUATION 
After training, the performance of the YOLOv8l model was evaluated using standard 
object detection metrics. The model was tested on unseen images from the testing dataset 
to measure its detection capability and generalization performance. The major evaluation 
metrics used in this project are listed below: 
• Precision (P): Measures the accuracy of positive detections. 
• Recall (R):  Measures the ability to detect all relevant objects present in the 
dataset.
